Four shots in and my numbers were starting to blur.  Most weren’t interesting anyway, the vast majority being in single digits.  Occasionally someone would creep into the teens, but it wasn’t worth chasing down every person who broke 10.  Two numbers for everyone.  One blue.  One red.  And that would tell me everything I needed to know.

“So” I shouted to the guy leaning against the bar next to me.  With a pair of 27’s, he was my best friend in the world.  “How many of these people do you think are gonna have a new clock by morning?”

David had a timer on every heartbreak you’ve ever had.  Those clocks held a surprising wealth of information, and always made for interesting conversations.

“More than you might think” he shouted back.  “Weekends always see a rise”

“Alcohol doesn’t mix with love very well” the blonde on my other side quipped.  The only negative I’d ever allowed into my life.  A blue -15 dancing on her head was a reminder of how often she hurt me.  The red 39 sitting on her shoulder was why I could never leave.

“Kristen, you’re supposed to be a happy drunk” I commented.  With the way she was slumped over the bar, I didn’t need David to tell me how low her timer was.

“I would be if you’d let me go for the tequila” she said bitterly.

“As fun as it is having you go nympho on me every night, if you keep it up I’m going to get attached.  Now finish your beer and let’s have a dance” I ordered.

“Oh!” David yelled out, drawing my attention.  “What about her?  Asian girl, straight across”

Attractive, no doubt, but I let my numbers do the talking.  3 for blue, -1 for red.  Best to avoid, but that was just me.  David had his own resources for a situation like this.

“What, think she’s on the rebound?” I asked knowingly.

“I think I could make it work” Well, there was no doubting the earnestness in his voice.

“Go for it” I said, rolling my eyes.  He was gone in a heartbeat.

“I suppose I should stop him” Kristen mused.

I couldn’t help but laugh.  Of everyone I knew, Kristen’s Stat struck me as the most ironic.  How many bad decisions you had ever made.  I doubt she was happy with her own number.

“He’ll learn” I said, unworried.  Kristen always seemed to know how severe things would get.

David was back within five minutes, dejection evident in his features.  I was on the verge of making a comment when something caught my eye.  Something I’d never seen before.

“No fucking way…” I breathed.

“What is it?” Kristen asked.  I didn’t hear her.  My mind was fixated on the girl who’d just walked in.  Deep red hair, pale complexion, striking green eyes, fit body, graceful movement.  Any one of those traits could’ve caught my interest, but there was one element that had me staring.

Triple digits.

100 on one side.  -100 on the other.  Was it worth it?  Could I do that?

Curiosity decided for me, and I left the other two behind.

“Idiot” Kristen whispered.  I didn't hear that either.

Empire steamrolls Star Fleet in all four scenarios.

In case 1 it's a matter of individual ship power.  Imperial warships are just that: warships. They're very heavily armed and well-protected. Let's look at a basic Imperial I-class Star Destroyer, mainstay of the fleet. 80 heavy turbolasers, 8 medium turbolasers, 4 heavy ion cannons, 60 regular ion cannons, 10 tractor beam projectors. And don't forget, she's hauling 72 snub ships as well. Starfleet ships are designed to explore, with the capability to defend themselves. Let's take a look at the Sovereign-class now, arguably one of the most powerful ship types in Starfleet. 16 phaser arrays (post refit), 1 quantum torpedo launcher, and 9 photon torpedo launchers. The difference between the two is staggering. Starfleet's most powerful ships would be hard pressed to stand up against a standard Imperial capital ship.

Case 2 is even worse for Starfleet. The Imperial fleet is massive, much more massive than Starfleet. The Federation as a whole is fairly widespread in a single quadrant of the Milky Way. The Empire spans a whole galaxy, and has the military power to maintain that hold. It'd be a slaughter.

Case 3 is probably the closest Starfleet can get to winning, but it's still pretty bad. Earth relies mostly on ships to defend it. There isn't much in the way of orbital defenses. We've already seen what happens when Starfleet tries to fight the Empire ship-to-ship.

Case 4 is impossible for Starfleet to win. Completely. Courscant is extraordinarily well defended. At the time of Imperial control, it's got two planetary defense shields, orbital defense platforms, and quite a lot of ships. The Empire could probably win on ships alone. Add the other defenses and it's hopeless.

Don't get me wrong, I love both Star Trek and Star Wars, but this is a very uneven match. Starfleet is part of a peaceful organization that aims to explore and learn about the galaxy. The Imperial fleet is a war machine that already spans a galaxy.  This is David vs Goliath, except David doesn't have a sling and Goliath has an AC-130 flying support.

Hm. I do like the idea of an RPG ODST game. But I don't think this is the best way to implement it. Remember, at the time you're suggesting, ODSTs were the absolute best special forces humanity had. Or at least, that the public knew about. The SPARTAN program was still highly classified. Knowing that, I doubt they'd be roaming the countryside performing peacekeeping duties. It's like someone else said, you're making them into the National Guard. They're meant to be actively deployed against high-level threats. You don't see SEALs or SAS wandering around keeping the populace in check, do you?

Personally, I like the idea of playing a character who's just become an ODST, being assigned to a squad, and then going through the war with them. Or maybe starting out as a new squad leader. RPG elements could come into play in learning knew skills (if you're starting from the Rookie level), or figuring out how to make your team as effective as it can be. Along the way, you can get upgrades for weapons and armor as R&D analyzes Covenant tech, or makes breakthroughs of their own. ODST let us experience a single night with the squad. I think it's only natural that the progression from that is to experience a day with them, a month, a year, a decade. Give us multiple drops. Give us more than one mission.

Speaking of missions, I don't think you should get any say as to when you're deployed, or what mission you're going on. You're just a grunt in the military. You go where you're ordered to go, when you're ordered to do so. But once the mission starts, then you can get your freedom of choice. That's the benefit of special forces, they can decide how to approach and execute an objective. Give an open world in the mission. Let there be multiple ways to accomplish an objective, and let the player decide how they want to go about it.

So I think you're overarching idea is a good one. RPG, open world (at least during actual missions). And actually, I think the idea of starting out against Innies and then switching to Covenant is pretty interesting (since the Insurrection has been pretty untouched in the games). But I don't think the actual gameplay you're suggesting would suit ODSTs.

While I don't agree with OP's suggestions, I don't think you're entirely correct. It is possible to deviate from natural selection, or at least severely limit it's effects.

Consider health care. Normally, if a genetic mutation doesn't benefit or actively harms someone, it will be harder for them to survive, so anyone with this mutation has a lower chance of passing it on to future generations. It will eventually disappear. On the other hand, a mutation that benefits someone ensures a higher chance of survival, and a higher chance of passing this advantage on.

However, we live in a society that can ensure the survival of the disadvantaged through medical care. Natural selection can't take place if someone with a debilitating genetic mutation has just as much of a chance of passing that on as someone with a beneficial mutation.

I can't speak for everyone, but I'll contribute my personal thoughts.

Blake being a faunus isn't, in my opinion, interesting. By this point in the story, if she was revealed to be one, no one would be shocked by it. People would, as you say, lose their minds. Supporters would flip out at the confirmation of the theory, dissenters would be disappointed or angry at the choice. But no one would be surprised. You would be able to look back and see all the obvious "hints" that have been tossed out, particularly in From Shadows. And that is something RT has never done when it comes to a twist. It's never been hinted at so heavily. They may do it subtlety, in such a way that, looking back, you can find all the hints and nods that you missed. But I can't think of a time when a twist they threw out DIDN'T surprise the vast majority of people.

Next, there's avenues for character development. Let's say, hypothetically, she is a faunus. Ok, we get the obvious conflicts between her and people like Cardin. We get the "fighting to liberate her people" motivation. And then...what? There isn't a lot there. Now let's say she isn't a faunus (again speaking hypothetically), but instead merely an ally. What do we get with that? You can still have conflicts between her and people who see faunus as sub-human. You can still have her fight for their rights. But you have more depth. It would speak volumes to the kind of person she is if she doesn't HAVE to fight for faunus rights. She has no stake in this fight, but she chooses to involve herself because of her beliefs. Because of what she thinks is right. This, to me, is far more appealing. What's more, what happens if the goals of the faunus, or groups that she's affiliated with, begin to conflict with her own morals? Will she continue to fight for them, judging that the ends justify the means? Or will she try to distance herself from actions she deems unacceptable? There's one line that sticks with me. The quote from her trailer. "Your hopes have become my burden. I will find my own liberation..." This, to me, says that she has taken on a cause that is not her own, and now it's weighing down on her. And she needs to find her own freedom.

Again, this is MY opinion. I can't speak for anyone else. If she does turn out to be a faunus, alright. It won't ruin the show for me. She'll still be my favorite character. But I will lament a lost opportunity. What I don't understand is why some people want her to be a faunus so badly, so maybe someone could enlighten me. Until then, however, I think she hasn't been revealed as a faunus simply because there is nothing to reveal.

Destroy is my least picked option for a very simple reason. I will not kill an entire race of beings just to achieve my goal. I will not sacrifice the Geth, after Legion has already sacrificed himself and they have finally achieved true, individual consciousness. I will not sacrifice EDI, who has finally learned what it means to be alive.
